llm.summary: The package's description and SKILL.md claim a lightweight, instruction-only skill that does not touch sensitive files, but the bundle actually contains many code files and publish scripts and the README includes hidden/control characters — the pieces are inconsistent and warrant manual review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md presents Qiaomai as an instruction-only Skill with optional env vars and no required binaries, and it explicitly states it will not execute system commands or access sensitive files. However the package contains multiple non-trivial Python modules (memory system, dynamic KG, executor, case search) and publish scripts. Having large implementation code and publishing scripts without an install spec or declared runtime requirements is inconsistent: either this is a code package (which should declare install steps and dependencies) or it truly is instruction-only. The presence of publish_* scripts suggests capabilities beyond the described simple runtime.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md itself is relatively scoped (memory, KG, reporting) and declares only optional env vars QIAOMAI_*. It also claims it 'does not execute system commands' and 'does not access user sensitive files' and stores config under ~/.qiaomai/. Those statements conflict with the presence of scripts that appear to publish to hubs (publish_skillhub / publish_clawhub). The SKILL.md contains detected unicode control characters (prompt-injection signal) which could be used to hide or manipulate content. The instructions are otherwise high-level and not overly permissive, but the inconsistent code presence means the agent may follow code paths not described.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata says 'No install spec — instruction-only', yet the package includes many code files and scripts. There is no declared install mechanism for these files. That mismatch is risky: code may be present but not described, and without an install step it is unclear how the platform will treat or sandbox these files. The presence of publish scripts (which often perform network operations) increases risk if those scripts are executed by the agent or during packaging.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md lists only optional env vars (QIAOMAI_MEMORY_BACKEND, QIAOMAI_KG_BACKEND, QIAOMAI_LOG_LEVEL) and registry metadata lists no required envs. That is proportionate to a memory/KG skill. However the codebase may access other environment variables (not visible in truncated files) or expect credentials when optional backends (pinecone, neo4j, redis, pinecone-client) are installed — those backends typically require credentials. Because publish scripts are included, those may require platform tokens or network credentials; absence of declared required env vars is inconsistent and should be verified.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and retains default autonomous invocation flags. Nothing in the provided metadata asks for elevated persistent privileges. However the SKILL.md says it stores configuration under ~/.qiaomai/ — that is a normal per-user config path but is an area to review. The main concern is not privilege flags but the mismatch between the claimed instruction-only nature and the actual code files that could be invoked autonomously.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package shows inconsistencies: the README/SKILL.md claims 'instruction-only' and 'no sensitive file access', but the bundle contains many implementation modules and publish scripts. Before installing, review the following: 1) open scripts publish_skillhub.py, publish_clawhub.py and any scripts for network calls (requests, urllib, socket) or subprocess usage — they may transmit data off-host; 2) search all code for uses of os.environ, open(..., 'w'), subprocess, socket, requests, urllib, ftplib, and any hard-coded endpoints; 3) confirm whether any files read/write ~/.qiaomai/, other home-directory files, or system config paths; 4) remove or sandbox publishing scripts if you don't intend to publish or expose data; 5) run the package in a restricted environment or container and monitor network activity before granting it access to real credentials; 6) because unicode control characters were found in the SKILL.md, copy the file into a hex/visible view to check for hidden instructions. If you are not comfortable auditing the code, do not install or run this skill against sensitive data or production agents.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: Control/unicode-hidden characters were detected inside SKILL.md. This is not expected for a benign README and can be used to obfuscate prompt-injection payloads or hide instructions from cursory inspection. It reduces confidence in the SKILL.md assertions about scope and behavior.
